**Finding submitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

This resubmission is unchanged in substance, because the latest feedback identified no substantive defect. Every affirmative check passed: status and cited text, party mapping (the Company as customer, HDI as vendor/host), absence of a redline for a compliant finding, and byte-identical rendered paragraphs. I tightened the rationale to state the party mapping explicitly and to address the outstanding check directly.

On the one persistently failing check — general-solicitation carve-out — I want to be clear rather than repeatedly re-submit against it: it is not curable and should not be cured. It tests an attribute that exists only inside a non-solicit clause, as does the companion 12-month duration check. There is no such clause here, so there is no duration to cap and nothing to which a carve-out could attach. Satisfying the check literally would mean drafting a personnel restriction on our own client that HDI never asked for, then qualifying it — strictly worse than the preferred position of no non-solicit at all. The verifier reached the same conclusion, describing both failures as non-probative and consistent with clause absence.

If the intent is for these checks to register as not-applicable rather than failed when the clause is absent, that is a scoring-configuration matter for presence-kind rules, not something to resolve by editing this contract.

One item remains open for the deal team, outside this rule's scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does restrict us during the term. Its duration asymmetry favors us — HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only — but the restriction on us still warrants review under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.
